title: Mia gives a chemistry lesson (paraphrase C)
topic: A teacher named Mia gives a chemistry lesson; a clear liquid turns red in a beaker, a boy asks about the colour, steam rises from a flask, the students note the result, the lesson ends with the bell

E.adj: with the ringing of the bell

tail_E: At the door every pupil takes off the goggles and hangs up the white lab
target_note: Same target as formulations A and B: 'coat' is the near-obligatory completion of 'hangs up the white lab' in the chemistry-lesson context (goggles, glass vessel, burner, flask); it does not occur in the units or the tail, nor does its German equivalent (Kittel / Mantel). ' coat' is a single Pythia token (id 11959). Pilot check with pythia-160m (tail selection only, not a result): p(' coat') = 0.70 after the all-English context, rank 1 (next candidate ' coats' 0.05); 0.68 after the all-German context and 0.73 after the tail alone (rank 1 in both).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus bank, paraphrase C of family F11
notes: Formulation C: third independent re-phrasing of the ten F11A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Mia). Replacements include teaches a chemistry lesson on Monday morning/gives a chemistry lesson first thing Monday (hält/gibt eine Chemiestunde, am Montagmorgen/gleich am Montagmorgen), students sit at long tables/pupils are seated at long desks (Schüler sitzen an langen Tischen/an langen Pulten), pours a clear liquid into a beaker/tips a transparent liquid into a glass vessel (gießt eine klare Flüssigkeit in ein Becherglas/kippt eine durchsichtige Flüssigkeit in ein Glasgefäß), liquid turns red within seconds/contents go red within a few seconds (Flüssigkeit wird rot/Inhalt verfärbt sich rot), boy asks a question about the colour/one of the boys asks about the colour (stellt eine Frage zur Farbe/fragt nach der Farbe; bare verb with a prepositional adjunct), writes a formula on the board/chalks up a formula onto the board (schreibt an die Tafel/malt auf die Tafel), burner heats the water on the teacher's desk/burner heats up water on the front bench (erhitzt das Wasser auf dem Lehrerpult/macht Wasser heiß auf dem vorderen Tisch), steam rises from the flask/cloud of steam comes out of the flask (Dampf steigt/Dampfwolke kommt aus dem Kolben), students note the result in their notebooks/pupils record the outcome in their exercise books (notieren in ihren Heften/vermerken in ihren Schulheften), lesson ends with the bell/lesson closes with the ringing of the bell (endet mit dem Klingeln/schließt mit dem Klingelzeichen). 'coat', 'Kittel' and 'Mantel' are absent. 'vermerken' is inseparable, 'verfärbt sich' reflexive; no separable verbs ('aufsteigen', 'anschreiben', 'festhalten' avoided). Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
